scope: Theorem 2.1 (Noisy near-quadratic sampling) of the manuscript “Subpolynomial query complexity for well-conditioned log-concave sampling” (preprints/Subpolynomial-query-complexity-for-well-conditioned-log-concave-sampling-September-26-2026/article.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 139 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9e9a41553023f95e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 5. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix 0 < e < 1, an integer K0 ≥ 2, and t > 0 satisfying 40(K0 + 2)t < 1 4 . (2.3) There are constants and a dimension threshold depending only on e, K0, t with the following property. For every integer d above that threshold, put δ = d−e. One measurable randomized oracle procedure works for every F ∈ C2(Rd) with Lip(∇F) ≤ δ, every x ∈ Rd, and every 0 < r ≤ 1. Given evaluation access to g = ∇F, it uses at most polylog(d)δ−t evaluations of g on every execution and returns X = Xpre + 1 2G, where G ∼ N(0, Id) is independent of Xpre and of all queries, and W2  L(Xpre), νx,r ∗ N(0, 3 4Id)  ≤ polylog(d)δK0 D(x). (2.4) Consequently both W2(L(X), νx,r ∗ N(0, Id)) and ∥L(X) − νx,r ∗ N(0, Id)∥TV are at most polylog(d)δK0 D(x). All constants in these bounds are uniform in F, x, r. The procedure’s scalar parameters, shapes of its computations, and query cap are independent of x and of the primitive. It uses no evaluations of F itself.
